rationale:
Split into 5 children: 4 new lemmas plus 1 reuse of a comparator-accepted declaration.

Why split. The selected statement bundles, under one "for L¹-a.e. t", three logically independent conclusions. Each uses different fields of IsRectifiableTriple and different analytic ingredients:
- (a) null-measurability of M_t: field nullMeasurableSet, f measurable.
- (b) local integrability of θ on M_t: fields subset and integrableOn, |G| ≤ L, the co-area identity (CA).
- (c) a.e. strong measurability of ξ_t: field aestronglyMeasurable, G measurable, continuity of the interior product ι.
They share only the null transfer (NT), the conclusion of the sibling ae_transfer applied to (CA). Children may depend only on their own siblings, so (NT) enters children 1, 3 and 5 as an explicit hypothesis, copied verbatim from ae_transfer's frozen conclusion. The parent passed (CA) the same way.

Children. Each is stated for the whole slice M ∩ f⁻¹{t}, which is stronger and more reusable; M_t ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}.
- slice_null_measurable: (a) for M ∩ f⁻¹{t}. Parent Steps 2 (Borel kernel B), 3 and 5(a).
- exhaustion: reuse of the accepted cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion. Title, statement, Lean type, key steps and accepted proof are byte-identical, with a provenance note, as for fiw_ims_frame_sign in the parent decomposition. K_i := closure W_i replaces the hand-made rational-ball exhaustion of parent Step 1.
- slice_integrable (depends on exhaustion): (b) on M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K. Parent Steps 1–4 and 5(b). It uses |θ₀| (via ‖θ₀‖ₑ) instead of max(θ₀, 0), so it needs neither θ > 0, null-measurability of M, nor measurability of f or G.
- contraction_lipschitz: v ↦ ι(v) is (m+1)-Lipschitz. This is the algebraic core of parent Step 5(c). It isolates the Lean pitfall the parent flagged, re-confirmed here: TopologicalSpace (Λ^m →L (ℝ^P →L Λ^m)) fails to synthesize. It is plausibly reusable wherever ι(G/|G|) occurs, e.g. slice_identity.
- slice_orientation_aesm (depends on contraction_lipschitz): (c) for H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}). Parent Steps 2 (ξ̃), 3 and 5(c).
The node could be proved atomically, but then it would have to re-prove the exhaustion, which the split instead reuses. The split also isolates the instance pitfall, and every child is small and independently checked.

subproblems.title: For L¹-a.e. t the slice M ∩ f⁻¹{t} is H^m-null-measurable
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be H^{m+1}-null-measurable and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be Borel measurable. Write Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P) and L¹ for Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Assume the null-transfer property for (M, f): for every predicate p on ℝ^P that holds for H^{m+1}-a.e. x ∈ M (∀ᵐ x ∂(H^{m+1} restricted to M), p x), for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ the predicate p holds for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} (∀ᵐ x ∂(H^m restricted to M ∩ f⁻¹{t}), p x). Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ the set M ∩ f⁻¹{t} is H^m-null-measurable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)) → Measurable f → (∀ p : Eucl P → Prop, (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), p x) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t})), p x) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), NullMeasurableSet (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}) (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; ‖·‖ₑ is the extended norm (‖r‖ₑ = |r| ∈ [0, ∞) for r ∈ ℝ). Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P). L¹ := volume on ℝ. n := m + 1. For a measure μ and an arbitrary set S, μ⌞S := μ.restrict S; it is a measure for every S, (μ⌞S)(A) = μ(A ∩ S) for Borel A (Measure.restrict_apply), and μ(A ∩ S) ≤ (μ⌞S)(A) for every A (Measure.le_restrict_apply). 'p holds μ-a.e. on S' means ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ⌞S), p x. (NT) is the null-transfer hypothesis for (M, f): for every predicate p on ℝ^P with p(x) for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, p(x) holds for H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. x. In the parent node it is the conclusion of the sibling slicing_im_st_ae_transfer applied to the co-area identity, and enters here as a hypothesis because children may depend only on their own siblings. This is Steps 2 (the Borel kernel B), 3 and 5(a) of the parent proof (slicing_im_st_measure_fields), stated for the whole slice M ∩ f⁻¹{t}.
1. (Borel kernel.) M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, so there is a Borel set B ⊆ M with B = M Hⁿ-a.e. (NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq).
2. (x ∈ B holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.) Since B = M Hⁿ-a.e., Hⁿ⌞B = Hⁿ⌞M (Measure.restrict_congr_set). As B is Borel, x ∈ B for Hⁿ⌞B-a.e. x (ae_restrict_mem). Hence the predicate p(x) :⟺ x ∈ B holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.
3. (Transfer.) By (NT) applied to p there is a set of full L¹-measure of t such that x ∈ B for H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. x, i.e. (H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}))({x : x ∉ B}) = 0 (ae_iff). Fix such a t.
4. (The part outside B is null.) Put Y := {x : x ∉ B} ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{t}). By Measure.le_restrict_apply, H^m(Y) ≤ (H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}))({x : x ∉ B}) = 0, so H^m(Y) = 0 (nonpos_iff_eq_zero).
5. (Decomposition.) M ∩ f⁻¹{t} = (B ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ∪ Y. Indeed, if x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} then either x ∈ B, so x ∈ B ∩ f⁻¹{t}, or x ∉ B, so x ∈ Y; conversely B ∩ f⁻¹{t} ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} because B ⊆ M, and Y ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} by definition.
6. (Conclusion.) B ∩ f⁻¹{t} is Borel because B is Borel and f is measurable (f⁻¹{t} is Borel: hf (measurableSet_singleton t)), hence H^m-null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet). Y is H^m-null, hence H^m-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.of_null). A union of two null-measurable sets is null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.union). So M ∩ f⁻¹{t} is H^m-null-measurable for every t in the full-measure set of Step 3, which proves the claim. No measurability of M ∩ f⁻¹{t} is used anywhere: restriction to an arbitrary set is a measure. ∎
proof_key_steps: Borel B ⊆ M with B = M Hⁿ-a.e.; then x ∈ B holds Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (restrict_congr_set, ae_restrict_mem)
null transfer: for a.e. t, (H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}))({x ∉ B}) = 0, hence H^m({x ∉ B} ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = 0 (le_restrict_apply)
M ∩ f⁻¹{t} = (B ∩ f⁻¹{t}) ∪ ({x ∉ B} ∩ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = Borel ∪ H^m-null, hence H^m-null-measurable

subproblems.title: Exhaustion of an open set by compactly contained open sets
subproblems.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and every open set U ⊆ ℝ^P (= Eucl P) there is a sequence (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} of subsets of ℝ^P with two properties. (a) For every i, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds: W_i is open, closure(W_i) is compact and closure(W_i) ⊆ U. (b) Every compact K ⊆ U is contained in W_i for some i.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∃ W : ℕ → Set (Eucl P), (∀ i, CompactlyContainedOpen (W i) U) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ i, K ⊆ W i
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance: this child reuses the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion of DAG node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.exhaustion-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit cb89cc7f436bbfa9b474f73003fa9aa79ebad102, no dependencies). Its frozen Lean type, title, statement and key steps are copied byte-for-byte from that node. The proof below is that node's accepted proof, copied verbatim; it is self-contained. Use in slicing_im_st_measure_fields: it replaces the parent's rational-ball exhaustion (parent Step 1) and is consumed by the new child slice_integrable (slicing_im_st_mf_slice_integrable), Step 1, with K_i := closure(W_i).

Source: parent proof Step 1 (exhaustion). The parent's condition B̄_{1/i}(x) ⊆ U is expressed here through the extended distance to ℝ^P∖U, so no convention for dist(x, ∅) is needed. The index is shifted to avoid 1/0.

Notation: |x| is the Euclidean norm on ℝ^P = Eucl P. For x ∈ ℝ^P let d(x) := inf{edist(x, y) : y ∈ ℝ^P∖U} ∈ [0, ∞] (Lean: Metric.infEDist x Uᶜ). If U = ℝ^P then d ≡ ∞.

1. d is continuous (Metric.continuous_infEDist). Since ℝ^P∖U is closed (U is open), d(x) = 0 iff x ∈ closure(ℝ^P∖U) = ℝ^P∖U (Metric.mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero). In particular d(x) > 0 for every x ∈ U.
2. For i ∈ ℕ define W_i := {x : |x| < i} ∩ {x : (i+1)⁻¹ < d(x)}, where (i+1)⁻¹ ∈ (0, ∞).
3. W_i is open: it is the intersection of the preimages of the open sets (−∞, i) and ((i+1)⁻¹, ∞] under the continuous maps x ↦ |x| and d.
4. W_i ⊆ B̄_i(0), and B̄_i(0) is closed, so closure(W_i) ⊆ B̄_i(0). B̄_i(0) is compact because ℝ^P is proper, so closure(W_i) is compact as a closed subset of a compact set.
5. F_i := {x : (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ d(x)} is closed (d is continuous) and contains W_i, so closure(W_i) ⊆ F_i. Suppose some x ∈ closure(W_i) is not in U. Then d(x) = 0 by Step 1, while x ∈ F_i gives d(x) ≥ (i+1)⁻¹ > 0 (since i+1 < ∞), a contradiction. Hence closure(W_i) ⊆ U. Together with Steps 3 and 4, CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U holds for every i.
6. Let K ⊆ U be compact. If K = ∅ then K ⊆ W_0. Otherwise:
- K is bounded, so there is R ∈ ℝ with |x| ≤ R for all x ∈ K. Choose i₁ ∈ ℕ with i₁ > R.
- d is continuous and K is compact and nonempty, so d attains its minimum on K at some x₀ ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Since x₀ ∈ U, Step 1 gives m := d(x₀) > 0.
- Choose i₂ ∈ ℕ with (i₂)⁻¹ < m (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt).
- Put i := max(i₁, i₂). For x ∈ K we have |x| ≤ R < i₁ ≤ i and (i+1)⁻¹ ≤ (i₂)⁻¹ < m ≤ d(x), so x ∈ W_i. Hence K ⊆ W_i.
7. Steps 5 and 6 show that (W_i)_{i∈ℕ} has both required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: d(x) := infEDist(x, ℝ^P∖U) is continuous and vanishes exactly off U.
W_i := {|x| < i} ∩ {d > (i+1)⁻¹} is open.
closure W_i ⊆ closedBall(0,i) ∩ {d ≥ (i+1)⁻¹}, which is compact and contained in U.
A compact K ⊆ U is bounded and min_K d > 0, so K ⊆ W_i for large i.

subproblems.title: For L¹-a.e. t, θ is H^m-integrable on M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, M ⊆ U, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ such that θ is H^{m+1}-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, L ≥ 0, and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ and G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be arbitrary functions (no measurability assumed) with |G(x)| ≤ L for all x. Write Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P) and L¹ for Lebesgue measure on ℝ. Assume the co-area identity for (M, f, G): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_M |G| g dH^{m+1}; and the null-transfer property for (M, f): every predicate that holds for H^{m+1}-a.e. x ∈ M holds, for L¹-a.e. t, for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}. Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, θ is H^m-integrable on M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (L : ℝ≥0) (G : Eucl P → Eucl P), IsOpen U → M ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P))) → (∀ x, ‖G x‖ ≤ L) → (∀ g : Eucl P → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → AEMeasurable (fun t : ℝ => ∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))) (volume : Measure ℝ) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (∫⁻ x in M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}, g x ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))) ∂(volume : Measure ℝ) = ∫⁻ x in M, ‖G x‖ₑ * g x ∂(μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P))) → (∀ p : Eucl P → Prop, (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), p x) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t})), p x) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t} ∩ K) (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; ‖·‖ₑ is the extended norm (‖r‖ₑ = |r| ∈ [0, ∞) for r ∈ ℝ). Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P). L¹ := volume on ℝ. n := m + 1. For a measure μ and an arbitrary set S, μ⌞S := μ.restrict S; it is a measure for every S, (μ⌞S)(A) = μ(A ∩ S) for Borel A (Measure.restrict_apply), and μ(A ∩ S) ≤ (μ⌞S)(A) for every A (Measure.le_restrict_apply). 'p holds μ-a.e. on S' means ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ⌞S), p x. (CA) is the co-area hypothesis for (M, f, G): for every Borel g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], t ↦ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g dH^m dt = ∫_M ‖G‖ₑ g dHⁿ. (NT) is the null-transfer hypothesis for (M, f): for every predicate p on ℝ^P with p(x) for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, p(x) holds for H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. x. In the parent node it is the conclusion of the sibling slicing_im_st_ae_transfer applied to the co-area identity, and enters here as a hypothesis because children may depend only on their own siblings. This is Steps 1–4 and 5(b) of the parent proof (slicing_im_st_measure_fields), stated for the whole slice M ∩ f⁻¹{t}, with two simplifications: the compact exhaustion is the sibling exhaustion (the comparator-accepted cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion) instead of the rational-ball construction, and the nonnegative Borel modification of θ is |θ₀| (used through ‖θ₀‖ₑ) instead of max(θ₀, 0), so neither θ > 0 nor null-measurability of M is needed.
1. (Exhaustion.) By the sibling exhaustion (cmb_exists_compactly_contained_exhaustion) applied to the open set U there are W_i ⊆ ℝ^P (i ∈ ℕ) with CompactlyContainedOpen W_i U for every i and such that every compact C ⊆ U satisfies C ⊆ W_i for some i. Put K_i := closure(W_i). By CompactlyContainedOpen, K_i is compact and K_i ⊆ U; K_i is closed, hence Borel (isClosed_closure.measurableSet). Every compact C ⊆ U lies in some W_i ⊆ K_i (subset_closure). For x ∈ M we have x ∈ U (M ⊆ U), {x} is compact and {x} ⊆ U, so x ∈ K_i for some i; hence M = ⋃_i (M ∩ K_i).
2. (Borel version of θ on M.) For each i, θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K_i (hypothesis with K := K_i), in particular Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K_i)-a.e. strongly measurable (Integrable.aestronglyMeasurable; IntegrableOn θ S μ is Integrable θ (μ⌞S)). Since ℕ is countable and M = ⋃_i (M ∩ K_i), θ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff). Let θ₀ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk θ: θ₀ : ℝ^P → ℝ is strongly measurable (hence Borel) and θ = θ₀ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk).
3. (Transfer.) By (NT) applied to p(x) :⟺ θ(x) = θ₀(x), there is a set T₁ ⊆ ℝ of full L¹-measure such that for t ∈ T₁: θ = θ₀ H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e.
4. (Finite slice integrals.) Fix i ∈ ℕ. The function g_i := 1_{K_i}·‖θ₀‖ₑ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (Set.indicator (K_i) (fun y => ‖θ₀ y‖ₑ)) is Borel (Measurable.enorm, Measurable.indicator). Let J_i(t) := ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}} g_i dH^m. By (CA) with g := g_i, J_i is L¹-a.e.-measurable and ∫_ℝ J_i dt = ∫_M ‖G‖ₑ g_i dHⁿ. Now:
   (i) ‖G(x)‖ₑ ≤ L for every x, because |G(x)| ≤ L (enorm_le_coe, NNReal.coe_le_coe, coe_nnnorm). Hence ∫_M ‖G‖ₑ g_i dHⁿ ≤ ∫_M L·g_i dHⁿ = L·∫_M g_i dHⁿ (lintegral_mono; lintegral_const_mul' since L ≠ ∞).
   (ii) As K_i is Borel, ∫_M g_i dHⁿ = ∫_{K_i ∩ M} ‖θ₀‖ₑ dHⁿ (lintegral_indicator, then Measure.restrict_restrict) = ∫_{M ∩ K_i} ‖θ‖ₑ dHⁿ: indeed θ = θ₀ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. implies θ = θ₀ Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K_i)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset, M ∩ K_i ⊆ M), and the integrals of a.e.-equal functions agree (lintegral_congr_ae).
   (iii) ∫_{M∩K_i} ‖θ‖ₑ dHⁿ < ∞, because θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K_i (its HasFiniteIntegral component).
   Hence ∫_ℝ J_i dt ≤ L·∫_{M∩K_i} ‖θ‖ₑ dHⁿ < ∞ (ENNReal.mul_lt_top), and therefore J_i(t) < ∞ for L¹-a.e. t (ae_lt_top', using the a.e.-measurability of J_i).
5. (All i at once.) By ae_all_iff (ℕ countable), there is a set T₂ of full L¹-measure such that J_i(t) < ∞ for all i ∈ ℕ and all t ∈ T₂. Fix t ∈ T₁ ∩ T₂ (a set of full L¹-measure).
6. (Integrability on M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K_i.) Fix i and put S := M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K_i. Since S ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}, Step 3 gives θ = θ₀ H^m⌞S-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset).
   (i) θ₀ is strongly measurable, so θ is H^m⌞S-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr).
   (ii) As K_i is Borel, J_i(t) = ∫_{K_i ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{t})} ‖θ₀‖ₑ dH^m (lintegral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict) = ∫_S ‖θ₀‖ₑ dH^m (K_i ∩ (M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) = S, Set.inter_comm) = ∫_S ‖θ‖ₑ dH^m (lintegral_congr_ae with θ = θ₀ H^m⌞S-a.e.). Hence ∫_S ‖θ‖ₑ dH^m = J_i(t) < ∞, i.e. θ has finite integral for H^m⌞S.
   By (i) and (ii), θ is H^m-integrable on S. No measurability of M ∩ f⁻¹{t} is used: only the Borel set K_i is ever measured or restricted to first.
7. (Arbitrary compact K.) Let K ⊆ U be compact. By Step 1, K ⊆ W_i ⊆ K_i for some i, so M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K_i, and θ is H^m-integrable on M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K (IntegrableOn.mono_set). This holds for every compact K ⊆ U and every t in the full-measure set T₁ ∩ T₂, which proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: exhaustion sibling: compact K_i := closure W_i ⊆ U, every compact C ⊆ U lies in some K_i, M = ⋃_i (M ∩ K_i)
θ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff); θ₀ := its strongly measurable version
null transfer: for a.e. t, θ = θ₀ H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e.
co-area with g_i = 1_{K_i}‖θ₀‖ₑ and ‖G‖ₑ ≤ L: ∫ J_i dt ≤ L ∫_{M∩K_i} |θ| dHⁿ < ∞, so J_i(t) < ∞ for a.e. t and all i
J_i(t) = ∫_{M∩f⁻¹{t}∩K_i} |θ| dH^m < ∞ gives integrability on M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K_i, then on M ∩ f⁻¹{t} ∩ K by mono_set

subproblems.title: The interior-product operator v ↦ ι(v) = v♭ ∧ · from ℝ^P to L(Λ^m, Λ^{m+1}) is (m+1)-Lipschitz
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ. For v ∈ ℝ^P let ι(v) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘ (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ v)) : Λ^m → Λ^{m+1}, where Λ^k := Covector (Eucl P) k is the space of continuous alternating k-forms on ℝ^P (so ι(v)α = v♭∧α, (ι(v)α)(v₀,…,v_m) = Σ_i (−1)^i ⟨v, v_i⟩ α(v₀,…,v̂_i,…,v_m)). Then the map v ↦ ι(v), from ℝ^P to the space of continuous linear maps Λ^m → Λ^{m+1} with the operator norm, is Lipschitz with constant m + 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ), LipschitzWith ((m : ℝ≥0) + 1) (fun v : Eucl P => (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) m) (innerSL ℝ v)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|. For v ∈ ℝ^P, ι(v) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘L (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ v)) : Λ^m →L Λ^{m+1}, where Λ^k := Covector (Eucl P) k (continuous alternating k-forms on ℝ^P, operator norm) and Λ_k := NVector (Eucl P) k = Λ^k →L ℝ; by rfl, ι(v)α = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α) = v♭∧α. The norm on Λ^m →L Λ^{m+1} is the operator norm, and dist(A, B) = ‖A − B‖. This is the continuity part of Step 5(c) of the parent proof (slicing_im_st_measure_fields), made quantitative.
1. (Formula.) For v ∈ ℝ^P and α ∈ Λ^m, ι(v)α = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α) holds definitionally (rfl; ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM_apply). By ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply, ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply and innerSL_apply_apply, for every σ = (σ_0, …, σ_m) ∈ (ℝ^P)^{m+1}:
   (ι(v)α)(σ) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i • (⟨v, σ_i⟩ • α(removeNth i σ)).
2. (ι is additive in the difference.) For v, w ∈ ℝ^P: ι(v) − ι(w) = ι(v − w). By extensionality in α ∈ Λ^m and σ ∈ (ℝ^P)^{m+1} (ext α σ), and the pointwise description of subtraction of continuous linear and alternating maps, both sides evaluated at α and σ are, by Step 1, Σ_i (−1)^i • ((⟨v, σ_i⟩ − ⟨w, σ_i⟩) • α(removeNth i σ)), using ⟨v − w, σ_i⟩ = ⟨v, σ_i⟩ − ⟨w, σ_i⟩ (inner_sub_left), sub_smul, smul_sub and Finset.sum_sub_distrib. Do not derive this from linearity of smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m regarded as a continuous map: at this Mathlib pin, instance search fails for TopologicalSpace (Λ^m →L (ℝ^P →L Λ^m)) (checked), whereas the extensional computation (a simp only with the lemmas just listed) works.
3. (Linear bound.) For u ∈ ℝ^P: ‖ι(u)‖ ≤ (m+1)|u|. By ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound (the constant (m+1)|u| is ≥ 0) it suffices to show ‖ι(u)α‖ ≤ (m+1)|u|‖α‖ for all α ∈ Λ^m. By Step 1 and ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_alternatizeUncurryFin_le, ‖ι(u)α‖ = ‖alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ u).smulRight α)‖ ≤ (m+1)‖(innerSL ℝ u).smulRight α‖, and ‖(innerSL ℝ u).smulRight α‖ = ‖innerSL ℝ u‖·‖α‖ = |u|·‖α‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.norm_smulRight_apply, innerSL_apply_norm).
4. (Lipschitz.) For v, w ∈ ℝ^P: dist(ι(v), ι(w)) = ‖ι(v) − ι(w)‖ = ‖ι(v − w)‖ ≤ (m+1)|v − w| = (m+1)·dist(v, w) (dist_eq_norm, Steps 2 and 3). The real number (m+1) is the coercion of the constant ((m : ℝ≥0) + 1). By LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul, v ↦ ι(v) is LipschitzWith ((m : ℝ≥0) + 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: ι(v)α = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α) by rfl; expand with alternatizeUncurryFin_apply
ι(v) − ι(w) = ι(v − w) by ext α σ and inner_sub_left, sub_smul, smul_sub, Finset.sum_sub_distrib (not via continuity of smulRightL)
‖ι(u)‖ ≤ (m+1)|u| by opNorm_le_bound, norm_alternatizeUncurryFin_le, norm_smulRight_apply, innerSL_apply_norm
LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with constant (m : ℝ≥0) + 1

subproblems.title: For L¹-a.e. t the sliced orientation x ↦ ξ(x) ∘ ι(G(x)/|G(x)|) is a.e. strongly measurable for H^m on M ∩ f⁻¹{t}
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ. For k ∈ ℕ let Λ^k := Covector (Eucl P) k be the space of continuous alternating k-forms on ℝ^P and Λ_k := NVector (Eucl P) k = Λ^k →L ℝ the space of k-vectors (both with operator norms). Let M ⊆ ℝ^P, let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1} be a.e. strongly measurable for H^{m+1} restricted to M, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be an arbitrary function (no measurability assumed) and let G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be Borel measurable. Write Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P) and L¹ for Lebesgue measure on ℝ, and assume the null-transfer property for (M, f): every predicate that holds for H^{m+1}-a.e. x ∈ M holds, for L¹-a.e. t, for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ f⁻¹{t}. With ι(v) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘ (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ v)) (ι(v)α = v♭∧α), put ξ'(x) := ξ(x) ∘ ι(|G(x)|⁻¹G(x)) ∈ Λ_m (with |0|⁻¹·0 = 0). Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable for H^m restricted to M ∩ f⁻¹{t}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (f : Eucl P → ℝ) (G : Eucl P → Eucl P), AEStronglyMeasurable ξ ((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) → Measurable G → (∀ p : Eucl P → Prop, (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), p x) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t})), p x) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (ξ x).comp ((ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ (Eucl P) ℝ).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.smulRightL ℝ (Eucl P) (Covector (Eucl P) m) (innerSL ℝ (‖G x‖⁻¹ • G x))))) ((μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ f ⁻¹' {t}))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k), with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; ‖·‖ₑ is the extended norm (‖r‖ₑ = |r| ∈ [0, ∞) for r ∈ ℝ). Hᵏ := μHE[k] (Mathlib's Euclidean Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P). L¹ := volume on ℝ. n := m + 1. For a measure μ and an arbitrary set S, μ⌞S := μ.restrict S; it is a measure for every S, (μ⌞S)(A) = μ(A ∩ S) for Borel A (Measure.restrict_apply), and μ(A ∩ S) ≤ (μ⌞S)(A) for every A (Measure.le_restrict_apply). 'p holds μ-a.e. on S' means ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ⌞S), p x. (NT) is the null-transfer hypothesis for (M, f): for every predicate p on ℝ^P with p(x) for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, p(x) holds for H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. x. In the parent node it is the conclusion of the sibling slicing_im_st_ae_transfer applied to the co-area identity, and enters here as a hypothesis because children may depend only on their own siblings. For v ∈ ℝ^P, ι(v) := (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM ℝ ℝ^P ℝ) ∘L (smulRightL ℝ ℝ^P Λ^m (innerSL ℝ v)) : Λ^m →L Λ^{m+1}, where Λ^k := Covector (Eucl P) k (continuous alternating k-forms on ℝ^P, operator norm) and Λ_k := NVector (Eucl P) k = Λ^k →L ℝ; by rfl, ι(v)α = alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ v).smulRight α) = v♭∧α. Put ν(x) := |G(x)|⁻¹G(x) and ξ_t(x) := ξ(x) ∘L ι(ν(x)) ∈ Λ^m →L ℝ = Λ_m (the function does not depend on t; only the measure H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t}) does). This is Steps 2 (the Borel version ξ̃), 3 and 5(c) of the parent proof (slicing_im_st_measure_fields), stated for the whole slice M ∩ f⁻¹{t}.
1. (Borel version of ξ.) ξ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable. Let ξ₀ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk ξ: ξ₀ : ℝ^P → Λ_{m+1} is strongly measurable and ξ = ξ₀ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.stronglyMeasurable_mk, AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk).
2. (Transfer.) By (NT) applied to p(x) :⟺ ξ(x) = ξ₀(x), there is a set of full L¹-measure of t such that ξ = ξ₀ H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. Fix such a t.
3. (ν is strongly measurable.) G is Borel measurable, so x ↦ |G(x)|⁻¹ is measurable (Measurable.norm, Measurable.inv) and ν = |G|⁻¹ • G is measurable (Measurable.smul). As ℝ^P is second countable and metrizable, ν is strongly measurable (Measurable.stronglyMeasurable). (Where G(x) = 0, ν(x) = 0 by the convention 0⁻¹ = 0; no case distinction is needed.)
4. (ι ∘ ν is strongly measurable.) By the sibling contraction_lipschitz (slicing_im_st_mf_contraction_lipschitz), v ↦ ι(v) is ((m : ℝ≥0) + 1)-Lipschitz, hence continuous (LipschitzWith.continuous). So x ↦ ι(ν(x)) is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable).
5. (A strongly measurable representative.) Composition (A, B) ↦ A ∘L B, from (Λ^{m+1} →L ℝ) × (Λ^m →L Λ^{m+1}) to Λ^m →L ℝ, is continuous (Continuous.clm_comp applied to continuous_fst and continuous_snd; equivalently isBoundedBilinearMap_comp.continuous). The pair x ↦ (ξ₀(x), ι(ν(x))) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.prodMk of Steps 1 and 4). Hence F(x) := ξ₀(x) ∘L ι(ν(x)) is strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable), in particular H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.aestronglyMeasurable).
6. (Congruence.) At every x with ξ(x) = ξ₀(x) we have ξ_t(x) = ξ(x) ∘L ι(ν(x)) = ξ₀(x) ∘L ι(ν(x)) = F(x). By Step 2 this holds for H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. x, so F = ξ_t H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e., and ξ_t is H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr). This holds for every t in the full-measure set of Step 2, which proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: ξ₀ := strongly measurable version of ξ with ξ = ξ₀ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.; null transfer gives ξ = ξ₀ H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e. for a.e. t
ν = |G|⁻¹G is measurable, hence strongly measurable; ι continuous by the sibling contraction_lipschitz, so ι∘ν is strongly measurable
F(x) = ξ₀(x) ∘L ι(ν(x)) strongly measurable via Continuous.clm_comp and StronglyMeasurable.prodMk
ξ' = F H^m⌞(M ∩ f⁻¹{t})-a.e., so ξ' is a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.congr)
